_comment: Hand-written table for provider_nebius. Contract: `.claude/skills/lease/references/contract.md`
'Shape resolution' — and specifically its rule 'Put in the table only what the API will not
tell you'. Nebius serves gpu_count, vCPU, host RAM and GPU memory live from
`capacity resource-advice list`, so none of those are here; duplicating them would create a
second author for a value that already has one, and the stale copy is the one that gets read.
What is left is what no Nebius API returns: compute capability, a human GPU name, and price.
PROVENANCE IS PER FIELD AND IS NOT DECORATION. `arch` is a hard admission check — a wrong
value either refuses a machine that would have worked or admits one whose kernels will not
load — so an inferred value must not read like a measured one. `arch_status`: `verified` = a
job was actually built and run for it on this platform; `claim` = inferred from the card name
and not yet confirmed here.
There is no per-hour price query in the Nebius API (billing v1alpha1 offers only `calculator`
and `one-time-export`), so every price here is somebody reading a console page on the date in
`price_asof`. That makes all of them `claim`, and `capacity` labels them so — a fleet cost
estimate quoted off this file is an estimate off a note, and must be said as one.
`price_gpu_hr: null` means nobody wrote it down; it never means free.

gpu-h100-sxm.note: the reference platform — started first try on every attempt in eu-north1

gpu-h200-sxm.note: same Hopper generation as H100, 141GB HBM3e

gpu-l40s-a.note: on-demand stock in eu-north1 has been persistently zero while quota reads fine; the preemptible pool is where this card is actually obtainable

gpu-l40s-d.note: multi-GPU presets; same card as gpu-l40s-a, different host shape

gpu-b200-sxm.note: Blackwell — a torch built for cu121 will not load here; see the contract's arch paragraph

gpu-gb300.note: Grace-Blackwell; the host is aarch64, so an x86 wheel set does not apply

gpu-rtx6000.note: 96GB variant, so Blackwell rather than the 48GB Ada part

_comment_native_ttl: false, and the substitute is only half a switch on this provider — say so rather than let
a caller assume Money rule 3 is fully covered. The guest-side `shutdown -h +N` stops the
compute burn, which is the large number, but leaves the instance STOPPED with its boot disk
still billing. `/lease reap` is what finishes it, and it is why reap belongs at conversation
start rather than being an occasional chore.
‼️ And the guest switch does not work at all under the DEFAULT recovery policy. The API docs
for --recovery-policy are explicit: an instance undergoing a guest shutdown 'will be subject
to recovery policy, meaning that it could be restarted and billed accordingly'. Default is
`recover`. So a box armed with `shutdown -h` and left at the default comes back up, empty,
and bills forever — a dead-man switch that reads as armed and is worse than none, because
nobody re-checks a safety they believe in. provider_nebius passes `--recovery-policy fail`
unconditionally for this reason, not only for the preemptible case that also requires it.

defaults._comment_image: driver + CUDA preinstalled. A driverless image has no nvidia-smi, which makes every capacity and health probe in this layer return nothing on a machine that is fine.

_comment: THE SECOND METER. A disk starts billing when it is created, keeps billing while the
instance is STOPPED, and survives the instance being deleted whenever it was not a
managed boot disk. `sweep` enumerates them for that reason; this table is where their
price would live.
Every price here is null, and that is a measurement status, not a placeholder to be
filled with a guess. Nebius publishes no per-hour storage price through the API (the
same gap as compute: billing v1alpha1 offers only `calculator` and `one-time-export`),
and nobody has read a console page for it. Per the contract's 'Shape resolution',
null means nobody wrote it down and NEVER means free -- `lease.py` counts an unpriced
row and reports the total as a lower bound, which is the honest rendering of a volume
whose size is known and whose rate is not.
Fill a rate here only from a console page, with the date, and it stays a `claim`.
